summary: This experimental RFC describes boundary-node behavior for the Controlled Load mode of Pre-Congestion Notification, a measurement-based load control approach using three marking states: not-marked, threshold-marked and excess-traffic-marked.

eli5.summary: The entry and exit guards watch warning colors and use them to decide whether to let more cars in or stop some.

questions: what is pcn controlled load mode
how do pcn boundary nodes behave in cl mode
what is the congestion level estimate in pcn
how does pcn decide to terminate flows
subtitle: How edge nodes use three marking states to admit new flows and terminate existing ones before a network congests.

tldr.problem: Voice and video flows cannot adapt when a network gets overloaded. A Diffserv domain needs a simple, scalable way to protect admitted flows, including in abnormal cases such as rerouting after a failure.
tldr.mechanism: Interior nodes mark PCN packets as not-marked, threshold-marked or excess-traffic-marked. Egress nodes measure the marked rates and report to a Decision Point, which compares a congestion level estimate to a limit to admit or block flows, and terminates flows when excess-traffic marking persists.
tldr.outcome: It is an Experimental RFC, published to validate and evaluate the Controlled Load edge behavior. A companion, RFC 6662, specifies the Single Marking alternative.

today: RFC 6661 is an Experimental RFC and is not obsoleted or updated according to the metadata. The Single Marking alternative is in RFC 6662.

sections.title: Introduction and the Experiment
sections.content:
Pre-Congestion Notification (PCN) aims to protect the quality of service of inelastic flows in a Diffserv domain. It uses two mechanisms: admission control, which decides whether to admit or block a new flow, and flow termination, which decides in abnormal circumstances whether to end some existing flows. Packets are marked when configured rates, set below the link rate, are exceeded, so edge nodes learn about incipient overload before any congestion occurs.

This document describes an experimental edge-node behavior, known as the Controlled Load (CL) mode. The experiment aims to validate the specification, evaluate how well it preserves quality of service, and assess whether PCN can reduce capital and operational costs compared with other methods. The text suggests a month or two in busy season may be enough for the first two goals. A companion document, RFC 6662, covers the Single Marking mode and shares much of this text.
sections.eli5: A warning system tells the gatekeepers that a road is getting full before it is jammed, so they can stop letting more cars in.

sections.title: Assumed Core Behavior and Roles
sections.content:
CL mode assumes that interior nodes perform both threshold-marking and excess-traffic-marking according to RFC 5670, using the codepoints defined in RFC 6660. On each link the threshold-meter's reference rate equals the PCN-admissible-rate, and the excess-traffic-meter's reference rate equals the PCN-supportable-rate.

The egress node collects the rates of not-marked, threshold-marked and excess-traffic-marked traffic per ingress-egress-aggregate and reports them. The ingress node enforces admission and termination decisions and reports the rate it sends when asked. The Decision Point makes the decisions and MAY be collocated with the ingress node. The signaling protocol for reports is out of scope.
sections.eli5: Road sensors paint cars with two kinds of warning marks. Exit guards count marks, entry guards let cars in, and a boss decides who goes.

sections.title: Egress Reporting and Report Suppression
sections.content:
The Decision Point is the node that decides which flows to admit and terminate; it can be the ingress node or a centralized node. The egress node meters each ingress-egress-aggregate over a period of length T_meas and computes NM-rate, ThM-rate and ETM-rate in octets per second. The congestion level estimate (CLE) is the ratio of PCN-marked to total PCN-traffic in octets.

The egress node SHOULD calculate the three rates at the end of each measurement period. Unless report suppression is activated, it MUST report them to the Decision Point each time. As an option it MAY also record identifiers of PCN-flows that saw excess-traffic marking, which helps avoid ending flows that are not on a congested path when multipath routing is used.

Report suppression MUST be available as a configurable option. When it is on, the egress node computes CLE = (ThM-rate + ETM-rate) / (NM-rate + ThM-rate + ETM-rate) and reports only if the latest or previous CLE exceeds the CLE-reporting-threshold (default zero), or if T_maxsuppress has elapsed since the last report. That guarantees a periodic sign of life.
sections.eli5: Exit guards report how many cars had each flag. To save chatter, they may stay quiet when all is calm, but they must still check in now and then.

sections.title: Admission and Termination at the Decision Point
sections.content:
For admission, the Decision Point takes the reported or calculated CLE and compares it to the configurable CLE-limit. If the CLE is less than the limit, the state for that aggregate is set to "admit"; otherwise it is "block". New flows SHOULD be admitted only in the admit state.

For termination, when a report shows a non-zero ETM-rate, the Decision Point asks the ingress node for its PCN-sent-rate and waits for the next egress report. If that report also shows a non-zero ETM-rate, it estimates the sustainable aggregate rate as SAR = NM-rate + ThM-rate and terminates traffic equal to PCN-sent-rate - SAR. It SHOULD first consider flows on the egress node's excess-marked list, and it is RECOMMENDED to wait between termination rounds so earlier terminations show up in the measurements.
sections.eli5: If too many cars are flagged, the gate closes to new cars. If the road really is overloaded, the boss sends some cars off the road, only as many as needed.

sections.title: Missing Reports and Timers
sections.content:
The Decision Point SHOULD run a timer t_recvFail that resets whenever a report arrives. It expires at T_fail, which is T_crit without suppression (or when the last CLE was above the reporting threshold) and 3 * T_maxsuppress otherwise. On expiry it SHOULD notify management, and local policy may block new flows to that egress node.

If a centralized Decision Point gets no answer about the PCN-sent-rate, it SHOULD repeat the request once. While waiting it MAY use ETM-rate as an over-estimate of the amount to terminate, and so SHOULD terminate less than the full amount at first. If the second request also fails, it MUST select flows using that approximation and SHOULD notify management.

Recommended values: T_meas on the order of 100 to 500 ms, T_maxsuppress on the order of 3 to 6 seconds, and T_crit not less than 3 * T_meas with a reasonable upper bound on the order of 3 seconds. They are based on judgement rather than operational experience.
sections.eli5: If a guard goes silent too long, the boss raises the alarm. If the entry guard does not answer, the boss asks once more, then makes a careful guess.

sections.title: Deployment, Management and Security
sections.content:
The RFC fills in the per-domain behavior template of RFC 3086. It applies to inelastic traffic such as voice and video and notes that CL is less likely than SM to terminate flows unnecessarily. The suggested service classes include Telephony (EF), Real-time interactive (CS4), Broadcast Video (CS3) and Multimedia Conferencing (AF4). The design requirement was recovery from overload by flow termination within 1-3 seconds.

Deployment involves choosing options and global parameters, deriving per-node and per-link information, installing but not activating parameters, and then activating and verifying behaviors. Filters to classify packets by ingress-egress-aggregate reliably require tunnels from ingress to egress node. Implementations MUST be able to log loss of contact, restored contact and flow termination events using syslog (RFC 5424), and counters are RECOMMENDED on all PCN nodes.

The security considerations of RFC 5559 apply. This memo adds one: with a centralized Decision Point, the interface on the ingress node used to communicate policy decisions is a point of vulnerability that must be protected from denial-of-service attacks. The Decision Point itself is a trusted entity.

IANA has added the syslog structured data IDs PCNNode and PCNTerm for event logs. The text also notes that PCN reuse of the ECN bits could theoretically interfere with end-to-end ECN.
sections.eli5: Before switching it on, the road crew sets up rules, installs sensors everywhere, tests them, and writes down every alarm in a logbook.
